mainTopic: Lessons from ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ for students, creditors and judges, then two clauses of the משנה on שבועת העדות: who is 'fit to testify,' and whether an oath outside בית דין counts.
overview: This amud teaches a long list of lessons from the פסוק ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״. It first finishes a case about a דיין who may not rule on a case he suspects is crooked and leave the blame on the עדים. Then a סימן lists nine more lessons. Three are about a תלמיד: he must not stay silent, must not delay correcting his רב, and must not even stand silently next to a lone witness. Three are about בעלי חוב who use false claims or false denials to win money that is really owed. Three are about fairness in court: equal dress, and no hearing one side, or speaking to the judge, without the other side present. רב כהנא gives another source for the last rule, and רב and שמואל explain ״וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא טוֹב עָשָׂה״. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. It asks who 'fit to testify' excludes, a מלך or a משחק בקוביא. It then explains that רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue over דון מינה ומינה versus דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.

steps.title: A judge cannot just blame the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: This line ends a case that began before this section. A דיין who senses a case is fraudulent may not rule anyway on the idea that the guilt will rest on the עדים. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and the blame will hang on the witnesses' necks? The verse teaches: 'Distance yourself from a false matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question that started earlier about a דיין who senses a case is crooked. It answers from the פסוק ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דיין might think: 'The עדים testified, so if it is false, the blame is on them.' The פסוק says no. A דיין must stay far from falsehood himself, so he cannot hand down a ruling he believes is wrong and blame others.

keyTerms.meaning: A chain or collar. Here it is a picture of carrying the blame.
Neck
'The verse teaches.' This introduces the source.
'Distance yourself from a false matter.' This is the source for every lesson here.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of a sentence that began earlier, about a דיין who suspects the case is a setup.

phrases.english: and the chain will hang on the neck of the witnesses?
phrases.notes: This finishes a question begun just before: a judge who senses fraud must not think the witnesses carry all the blame.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a case about a דיין that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A דיין who senses a case is fraudulent may not rule on it and leave the blame on the עדים.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן to help remember the next lessons from the same פסוק: three about a תלמיד, three about בעלי חוב, and three marked 'rags, hears, explain.'
steps.simpleTranslation: (Mnemonic: three about a student, three about creditors, and 'rags, hears, explain.')
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a short memory list of the lessons it is about to teach from ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סימן is not a ruling. It is a memory aid listing the order of the coming cases. The last three words are hooks for three more cases that the גמרא teaches in steps 11, 13 and 14.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign, a short list to help remember the order of teachings
Creditors, people who are owed money
Rags, worn-out clothing
Explains, makes his reasoning clear

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to learn a הלכה from the סימן itself. Each word only points to a case that is explained later.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: three — student,
and three — creditors,
rags, hears, and explain)
phrases.notes: These three words are memory hooks for three more cases coming up later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a list of more lessons from the same פסוק used in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling here. It is a memory list for the lessons that follow.

steps.title: A student may not stay silent
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד sitting before his רב who sees a point in favor of a poor person and against a rich person must not keep quiet. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a student sitting before his teacher, who sees a point in favor of the poor man and against the rich man, should not stay silent? The verse teaches: 'Distance yourself from a false matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first lesson about a תלמיד from the list. If he sees an argument that helps the poor side and hurts the rich side, he must speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying silent might not feel like lying, but it lets a wrong ruling go through. The פסוק says to stay *far* from falsehood, so even silence that allows a false outcome is not allowed. This holds even when he is sitting before his own רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?' A request for the source.
His teacher
A merit, an argument in someone's favor
He should not stay silent

phrases.english: From where do we know, regarding a student who sits before his teacher
and sees a merit for the poor man and a liability for the rich man —
from where do we know that he should not stay silent?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first of the three תלמיד cases listed in the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד who sees a point in favor of the poor party against the rich party must say it and not stay silent.

steps.title: A student may not wait in order to take the credit
steps.stepSummary: A תלמיד who sees his רב making a mistake in judgment may not wait until the ruling is finished, then overturn it and build his own ruling so the credit goes to him. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a student who sees his teacher erring in judgment should not say: 'I will wait until he finishes, then I will tear it down and build my own ruling, so the ruling will be called by my name'? The verse teaches: 'Distance yourself from a false matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second lesson about a תלמיד. He may not hold back his correction just so he can later overturn his רב's ruling and get the credit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the תלמיד plans to speak eventually, but only after the mistaken ruling is finished, for his own glory. The פסוק forbids letting a wrong ruling move forward even for a while. He must speak up right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Making a mistake in judgment
I will wait
I will tear it down, overturn it
I will build it up, construct a new ruling

steps.whatToRemember: All these lessons come from ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״. Being 'far' from falsehood means more than not lying. A דיין may not shift the blame to others, and a תלמיד may not stay silent or delay a correction.

phrases.english: From where do we know, regarding a student who sees his teacher
erring in the judgment, that he should not say:
I will wait for him until he finishes it;
and then I will tear it down and build it up from my own,
phrases.notes: He means he will overturn his teacher's ruling and put his own ruling in its place.

phrases.english: so that the ruling will be called by my name?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְתַלְמִיד שֶׁרוֹאֶה אֶת רַבּוֹ שֶׁטּוֹעֶה בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second תלמיד case from the סימן. It moves from total silence to delaying a correction for personal credit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד who sees his רב erring in judgment may not wait until the ruling is finished in order to overturn it and take the credit.

steps.title: A teacher asks his student to join a lone witness
steps.stepSummary: A רב who is sure he is owed money but has only one witness may not ask his תלמיד to join as a second witness. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? A רב says to his תלמיד: 'You know that even for a fortune I would never make up a claim. Someone owes me a מנה, but I have only one witness.' From where do we know the תלמיד may not join that witness? The פסוק says: ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last of the תלמיד lessons. A רב asks his תלמיד to help him collect a debt that the רב insists is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tricky part is that the רב is honest and the debt really exists. Even so, the תלמיד did not see the loan, so joining the witness would be false. The truth of the claim does not permit a false way of proving it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money worth one hundred דינרים
Make things up, invent a false claim
A single witness, which is not enough to make someone pay
Join together with, here as a second witness

phrases.english: From where do we know, about a student whose teacher said to him:
You know about me
that even if they gave me a hundred times a hundred dinars
I would not make up a claim;
so-and-so owes me a hundred dinars,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי עָלָיו אֶלָּא עֵד אֶחָד –
phrases.english: but I have only one witness against him –
from where do we know that the student may not join with him?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third in the series of תלמיד lessons listed in the סימן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד may not join his רב's single witness, even when the רב is certain the debt is real.

steps.title: Why do we need this verse, if testifying falsely is already forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it needs ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ here. A תלמיד who testifies about a loan he never saw is plainly lying, and that is already forbidden by ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn this from ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״? He is clearly lying, and the Torah already says: ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case from the previous step. It says the case already falls under the explicit commandment against false testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תלמיד actually testifies, he breaks one of the עשרת הדברות. A general warning to stay far from falsehood would add nothing. So the case must be some other kind of situation.

keyTerms.meaning: He is clearly lying
Literally 'the Merciful One'; the Torah or ה׳
A false witness

phrases.english: Is this learned from "Distance yourself from a false matter"?!
But he is certainly lying,
and the Torah says:
"You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor"!
phrases.notes: שמות 20:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which source the ruling in step 5 comes from
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ as the source for the lone-witness case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Actually testifying falsely is already forbidden by ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר״, so the general verse would add nothing.

steps.title: The student only stands there silently
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the רב asks the תלמיד only to stand next to the real witness and say nothing. Since he says no false words, ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה״ does not apply. It is still forbidden because of ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the רב said to him: 'I certainly have one witness. Just come and stand there and don't say anything, so no lie will come out of your mouth.' Even so it is forbidden, because it says ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the picture of the case. The תלמיד does not testify at all. He just stands there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing silently gives the false impression that there are two witnesses, which could push the borrower to admit. This is not false testimony in words, so ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה״ does not cover it. ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ forbids creating a false impression even without saying anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness
From your mouth
Even so

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תלמיד is lying out loud here. The whole point is that he says nothing. The silent false impression is what ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ forbids.
steps.whatToRemember: ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ goes beyond spoken lies. Even standing silently to create a false picture is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where he said to him:
I certainly have one witness,
and you, come stand there
and do not say anything at all,
since you will not be bringing a lie out of your mouth –
even so it is forbidden,
because it is stated: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by redefining the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תלמיד actually testifies, which is already forbidden by ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה״.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תלמיד only stands silently beside the witness. This is not covered by ״לֹא תַעֲנֶה״ but is forbidden by ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.

steps.title: A lender may not inflate his claim to force an oath
steps.stepSummary: A lender owed one מנה may not claim two, hoping the borrower will admit one. That admission would obligate the borrower in a שבועה, and the lender could then add other claims onto it. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that someone owed a מנה should not say: 'I'll claim two hundred. He'll admit to one hundred, become obligated to swear, and then I'll roll other claims onto his oath'? The פסוק says: ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the three lessons about בעלי חוב from the סימן. This first one is about a lender who exaggerates his claim on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who admits part of a claim (מודה במקצת) must take a שבועה. Once a person must swear, the other side can add other claims to that same oath (גלגול שבועה). The lender is owed real money, but he invents a false claim to set up this oath, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is owed money by his fellow; a lender
I will make a claim against him
One who admits part of a claim and must take a שבועה
Adding other claims onto an oath someone already has to take

phrases.english: From where do we know, about one who is owed a hundred dinars by his fellow,
that he should not say: I will claim two hundred from him –
so that he will admit to me one hundred,
and become obligated to take an oath to me,
and I will add onto his oath a claim from another place?
phrases.notes: Literally 'roll onto him an oath.' Once he has to swear, the lender tacks on other claims he couldn't make him swear about on their own.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לַנּוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר אֶטְעָנֶנּוּ בְּמָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תלמיד lessons to the first of the בעלי חוב lessons in the סימן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender may not inflate his claim to trigger a מודה במקצת oath and then use גלגול שבועה.

steps.title: A borrower may not deny in court and admit outside
steps.stepSummary: When a lender claims two hundred but is owed one hundred, the borrower may not plan to deny everything in בית דין and admit privately. His goal would be to avoid a שבועה and any added claims. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know about someone owed a מנה who claims two hundred, that the borrower should not say: 'I'll deny it all in בית דין and admit it to him outside, so I won't have to swear and he can't roll other claims onto my oath'? The פסוק says: ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second בעלי חוב lesson. Now the borrower is the one tempted to play games, this time to escape an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower admits one hundred in court, he becomes a מודה במקצת and must swear. He could also face גלגול שבועה. So he plans to deny it all in court and quietly pay outside. Even though he means to pay what he really owes, lying in בית דין is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I will deny his claim
Outside of court, privately

steps.whatToRemember: In these בעלי חוב cases someone is owed or owes real money. Even so, ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״ forbids using a false claim or a false denial to control the oath.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַנּוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה וּטְעָנוֹ מָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: From where do we know, about one who is owed a hundred dinars by his fellow and claimed two hundred from him,
that he should not say: I will deny his claim in court
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the borrower, not the lender.

phrases.english: and admit to him outside of court,
so that I will not become obligated to take an oath to him

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְגַלְגֵּל עָלַי שְׁבוּעָה מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר?
phrases.english: and he will not add onto my oath a claim from another place?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לַנּוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה וּטְעָנוֹ מָאתַיִם שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמַר אֶכְפְּרֶנּוּ בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second בעלי חוב lesson; the mirror image of step 8 from the borrower's side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower may not deny the debt in בית דין and admit it privately just to avoid a שבועה and גלגול שבועה.

steps.title: Three partners may not turn two of themselves into witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Three people owed a total of one מנה by one person may not have one act as the only claimant and the other two act as witnesses so they can collect and split it. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that if three people are owed a מנה by one person, one of them may not act as the claimant while the other two act as witnesses, so they can collect the מנה and split it? The פסוק says: ״Stay far from a false matter.״
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last of the בעלי חוב lessons from the סימן. Here three partners try to set things up so two of them can testify for the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debt is real, so nobody is inventing a loan. The falsehood is in the setup: the two "witnesses" act like neutral outsiders, but they each own a share of the money. Hiding their personal interest is a lie in disguise, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of money worth one hundred זוז
A litigant, one of the sides in a court case
And they will divide it
The פסוק teaches

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the three are lying about the debt. The money really is owed. What makes it false is that the two witnesses pretend to have no stake in the case when they actually do.

phrases.english: From where do we know, about three people who are owed a מנה by one person,
phrases.notes: The three together are owed one מנה, so each one owns a share of it.

phrases.english: that one should not act as the litigant
and the other two act as witnesses,
so that they collect the מנה and divide it?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third בעלי חוב lesson from the סימן, after steps 8 and 9. It is again about winning a true claim by dishonest means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners owed money may not present one as the sole claimant and the others as witnesses in order to collect and split it.

steps.title: Both litigants must be dressed alike in court
steps.stepSummary: If one litigant comes in rags and the other in a very expensive garment, בית דין tells the rich one to dress like the poor one or to dress the poor one like himself. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that when two people come to court, one in rags and one in a very expensive cloak, we tell the rich one: dress like him, or dress him like you? The פסוק says: ״Stay far from a false matter.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to fairness inside the courtroom. Two litigants must not look unequal in front of the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one side looks rich and important and the other looks poor, the judges may be swayed, or the poor man may feel too intimidated to argue well. Either way the ruling could come out false. So בית דין evens out their appearance first.

keyTerms.meaning: Rags, torn old clothes
A fancy cloak or robe
Dress like him

phrases.english: From where do we know, about two people who came to court,
one dressed in rags

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד לָבוּשׁ אִיצְטְלִית בַּת מֵאָה מָנֶה,
phrases.english: and one dressed in a cloak worth a hundred מנה,
that we say to him: Dress like him
phrases.notes: "Him" here is the rich litigant.

phrases.english: or dress him like you?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first of the last three cases in the סימן (סְמַרְטוּט). It shifts from dishonest claims by the litigants to how בית דין keeps the hearing fair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Litigants must appear equal in court. The rich one either dresses down or dresses the poor one up.

steps.title: רבא בר רב הונא makes litigants take off their fancy shoes
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא would tell litigants to take off their fine shoes before coming to judgment, putting the rule of equal appearance into practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: When people came before רבא בר רב הונא, he said to them: Take off your fancy shoes and come down for judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how one אמורא actually carried out the rule from the last step. This is a real-life example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even small signs of status, like fine shoes, could make one side look more important. רבא בר רב הונא removed these signs so both sides would stand as equals before the court.

keyTerms.meaning: Take off, pull off
Your fancy shoes
Come down for judgment

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: When people would come before רבא בר רב הונא,
he would say to them: Remove your fine shoes
and come down for judgment.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of equal dress being put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before judgment, litigants should remove fine clothing such as fancy shoes so neither looks more important.

steps.title: A judge may not hear one side before the other arrives
steps.stepSummary: A דיין may not listen to one litigant's arguments before the other litigant comes. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that a judge should not hear one litigant's words before the other litigant arrives? The פסוק says: ״Stay far from a false matter.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another rule for judges. The judge must hear both sides together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the judge hears one side alone, that story settles in his mind with no one there to answer it. He may lean toward it before he hears the other side, and his ruling could end up false.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge
His fellow, here the other litigant
Before he comes

phrases.english: From where do we know that a judge should not hear
the words of one litigant
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Without it, the line reads simply "the words of one litigant."

phrases.english: before the other litigant arrives?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְדַיָּין שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע דִּבְרֵי בַּעַל דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rules of courtroom fairness, now about when the judge may listen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge may not hear one litigant's claims unless the other litigant is present.

steps.title: A litigant may not present his case early to the judge
steps.stepSummary: A בעל דין may not explain his arguments to the דיין before the other litigant comes. The source is ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that a litigant should not lay out his arguments to the judge before the other litigant arrives? The פסוק says: ״Stay far from a false matter.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same rule from the other side. Now the litigant, not the judge, is warned not to speak to the judge alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step forbade the judge to listen. This step forbids the litigant to talk. Both lead to the same danger: a one-sided story could tilt the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain, present his reasoning in a convincing way (from טַעַם, a reason)
His words, his arguments

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְבַעַל דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יַטְעִים דְּבָרָיו לַדַּיָּין
phrases.english: From where do we know that a litigant should not explain his arguments to the judge
before the other litigant arrives?
The verse teaches: "Distance yourself from a false matter."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְבַעַל דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יַטְעִים דְּבָרָיו לַדַּיָּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 13: the same ban, aimed at the litigant instead of the judge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A litigant may not present his arguments to the judge when the other side is not there.

steps.title: רב כהנא learns it from a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns this rule from ״לֹא תִשָּׂא״ (do not accept a false report), reading it as ״לֹא תַשִּׂיא״ (do not cause others to accept one).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא teaches it from ״You shall not accept״ a false report, reading it as ״You shall not cause someone to accept.״
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא offers a different source for the rule just stated. He uses a פסוק about false reports instead of ״מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״לֹא תִשָּׂא״, "do not accept" a false report. רב כהנא also reads it as ״לֹא תַשִּׂיא״, "do not cause another to accept" one. A litigant who speaks to the judge alone makes the judge take in a one-sided story, so this reading fits the litigant's ban exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches, learns the rule from
Do not accept (a false report)
Do not cause someone else to accept

steps.whatToRemember: All these rules teach one idea: the truth must come out fairly. Partners may not disguise themselves as witnesses. Litigants must look equal. A judge hears both sides only together. רב כהנא adds that the litigant's ban can also come from ״לֹא תִשָּׂא״, read as ״לֹא תַשִּׂיא״.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one law can be rooted in more than one פסוק. רב כהנא's reading, ״לֹא תַשִּׂיא״, aims the warning directly at the person who causes the judge to hear a one-sided story.

phrases.english: רב כהנא teaches it from "You shall not accept"
phrases.notes: שמות 23:1, "You shall not accept a false report."

phrases.english: read as "You shall not cause to accept."
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels. Read this way, it warns you not to make someone else accept a false report.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the rule in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on a litigant presenting his case alone comes from ״לֹא תִשָּׂא״, read as ״לֹא תַשִּׂיא״.

steps.title: Who does 'what is not good among his people'
steps.stepSummary: רב says the פסוק refers to someone who comes to court with a הרשאה to argue for another person. שמואל says it refers to someone who buys a field that other people are fighting over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And did that which is not good among his people.' רב says: this is a person who comes to court with a power of attorney. שמואל says: this is a person who buys a field that people are contesting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more lesson about proper behavior around court cases, using a פסוק from יחזקאל. רב and שמואל disagree about who the פסוק is describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations describe a person who pushes into someone else's fight. For רב, it is the agent who takes on another person's lawsuit. For שמואל, it is the buyer who purchases a field while others are still arguing over it.

keyTerms.meaning: Power of attorney, written permission to argue someone else's case
People who contest or dispute ownership of something
He did what is not good

phrases.english: "And did that which is not good among his people":
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 18:18

phrases.english: Rav says: This is one who comes with authorization,
phrases.notes: He shows up in court with written permission to argue a case that isn't his own.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
This is one who buys a field
that has people contesting it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא טוֹב עָשָׂה בְּתוֹךְ עַמָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of lessons about behavior in court cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Getting involved in other people's disputes is called 'not good.' For רב this means an agent with a הרשאה, and for שמואל it means a buyer of a contested field.

steps.title: Who does 'fit to testify' come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that שבועת העדות applies only to people fit to testify. It asks which extra person this wording is meant to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the oath of testimony applies only to people fit to testify. What is that wording coming to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks a clarifying question about one of its phrases. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already lists people who cannot testify, such as relatives and disqualified people. So the general phrase 'fit to testify' must be adding someone new. The גמרא wants to know who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are fit to serve as witnesses
To exclude what? A question asking what a phrase leaves out
The oath of testimony, when a witness swears he knows nothing about a case

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא בִּרְאוּיִן לְהָעִיד כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: It applies only to those fit to testify, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. 'It' means the oath of testimony.

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the list of court-behavior lessons to analyzing the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person not explicitly listed in the משנה is excluded by the phrase 'fit to testify.'

steps.title: A king, or a dice player
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase excludes a מלך. רב אחא בר יעקב says it excludes a משחק בקוביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it excludes a king. רב אחא בר יעקב said: it excludes someone who plays with dice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers to its question. Each אמורא names a different person who is not 'fit to testify.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלך is not a relative and is not a wicked person, but he does not testify in court. A משחק בקוביא is a gambler whom the חכמים disqualified as a witness. Each אמורא holds that the person he names is not subject to שבועת העדות.

keyTerms.meaning: A king, who does not testify in court
One who plays with dice, a gambler disqualified as a witness

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
To exclude a king.
And Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
To exclude one who plays with dice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רב פפא the phrase excludes a מלך. According to רב אחא בר יעקב it excludes a משחק בקוביא.

steps.title: How far each opinion reaches
steps.stepSummary: The one who excludes a dice player would certainly exclude a king. The one who excludes a king might still include a dice player, because by Torah law the dice player is fit and only the רבנן disqualified him.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says a dice player is excluded, a king is excluded all the more so. According to the one who says a king is excluded, a dice player may not be excluded, because by Torah law he can testify, and it was only the רבנן who disqualified him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains whether the two opinions really disagree. The first opinion includes both people, while the second opinion may only include the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king cannot testify even by Torah law. So if a dice player, who is disqualified only by the רבנן, is excluded, the king surely is too. But someone who excludes only a king can say that the oath of testimony is a Torah law, so it follows the Torah's rules about witnesses, and by Torah law a dice player counts as a valid witness.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
By Torah law
He is certainly fit
They disqualified him

steps.whatToRemember: A משחק בקוביא is disqualified only by the רבנן. So it matters whether he is subject to the Torah-level שבועת העדות. A מלך cannot testify at all and is excluded according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a dice player is disqualified by the Torah. He is fit by Torah law, and that is exactly why one opinion may keep him subject to the oath.

phrases.english: The one who says one who plays with dice:
all the more so a king;
and the one who says a king:
but one who plays with dice,
by Torah law he is fit,
and it is the Rabbis who disqualified him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְשַׂחֵק בְּקוּבְיָא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the two answers of step 18 to show how far each one reaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone agrees a מלך is excluded. They disagree only about a משחק בקוביא, who is disqualified by the רבנן but fit by Torah law.

steps.title: What are רבי מאיר and the רבנן arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about an oath taken in front of בית דין or outside it. It asks what the root of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: in front of the court and not in front of the court, etc. What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks what the two sides are really arguing about. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר holds that a witness who swears on his own is liable even outside בית דין. The רבנן say he is liable only when he denies in court. The גמרא wants to find the underlying reason or source for each side.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of the court
About what do they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: In the presence of the court and not in the presence of the court, etc.
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה after finishing the 'fit to testify' discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying basis of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about liability for an oath taken outside בית דין.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: how far a comparison reaches
steps.stepSummary: Some חכמים said before רב פפא that רבי מאיר and the רבנן of the משנה argue over a method of learning. Is it 'learn from it, and take the details from it too,' or 'learn from it, but set the details in their own place'?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: They argue about whether we say 'learn from it and from it' or 'learn from it and set it in its own place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20 with a short headline. The next two steps will explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about the oath itself. It is about a rule of learning. When we learn one law from another, do we copy every detail of the source, or only the main point, filling in the details from the new topic's own rules?

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and from it: copy the main law and all its details from the source
Learn from it, but set it in its own place: copy the main law, but take the details from the new topic's own rules
They disagree
In front of him

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that we learn something from פקדון. They only argue about how much we learn: the main point alone, or the details too.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa:
Regarding 'learn from it, and from it,'
phrases.notes: Learn the law from the source, and take its details from that same source too.

phrases.english: versus 'learn from it, and set it in its own place,'
they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 about the root of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the רבנן about an oath taken in or outside בית דין?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about the method of learning: דון מינה ומינה versus דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר copies all the details from the deposit oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns two things from שבועת הפקדון. First, a witness who swears on his own is חייב. Second, he is חייב whether or not he swore in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: learn from פקדון, and take the details from it too. Just as with a deposit, one who swears on his own is liable, so too with testimony. And from it as well: just as with a deposit it makes no difference whether he swore in court or not, so too with testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's side. He compares שבועת העדות to שבועת הפקדון all the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first comparison teaches the main point: swearing on your own makes you liable. Because רבי מאיר holds דון מינה ומינה, he also copies the detail about place. A deposit oath works even outside בית דין, so a testimony oath does too.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit; here, the oath of someone who falsely denies holding another person's deposit
One who swears on his own, saying the oath himself
Liable, here to bring a קרבן

keyTerms.term: בֵּין בְּבֵית דִּין וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: Whether in court or not in court

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
Learn from it, and from it, from the deposit oath.

phrases.aramaic: מָה פִּקָּדוֹן – מוּשְׁבָּע מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Just as with a deposit, one who swears on his own is liable,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֵדוּת – מוּשְׁבָּע מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: so too with testimony, one who swears on his own is liable.
And from it as well:
phrases.notes: This is the second half of רבי מאיר's method: now the details also come from פקדון.

phrases.english: Just as with a deposit, whether in court
or not in court,
so too with testimony, whether in court
or not in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ מִפִּקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the headline given in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a witness who swears on his own is liable whether or not he swore in בית דין, because all the details are copied from פקדון.

steps.title: The רבנן take only the main point and keep the details from testimony
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן agree that a witness who swears on his own is חייב, just like with a deposit. But they take the 'place' detail from the rules of עדות itself. An oath imposed by others counts only in בית דין, so an oath taken on your own also counts only in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: learn from it, but set it in its own place. Just as with a deposit, one who swears on his own is liable, so too with testimony. But set it in its own place: just as one who is made to swear by others is liable in court and not outside court, so too one who swears on his own is liable in court and not outside court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן's side. They borrow only the main idea from פקדון and take the details from the rules of עדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the first comparison: swearing on your own makes you liable. The difference is where the details come from. The רבנן look back at the regular testimony oath, where others make you swear, which works only in בית דין, and apply that same limit to swearing on your own.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is made to swear by others; they say the oath and he accepts it
Set it in its own place: take the details from the topic's own rules
Yes
No

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי מאיר and the רבנן learn from פקדון that swearing on your own makes a witness liable. רבי מאיר also copies from פקדון that it works outside בית דין (דון מינה ומינה). The רבנן take the place rule from עדות itself, so it works only in בית דין (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This pair of methods, דון מינה ומינה and דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, comes up in other places in the גמרא. Here it shows clearly how one method decides a real practical difference.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
Learn from it, and set it in its own place.

phrases.aramaic: מָה פִּקָּדוֹן – מוּשְׁבָּע מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Just as with a deposit, one who swears on his own is liable,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֵדוּת – מוּשְׁבָּע מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: so too with testimony, one who swears on his own is liable.
But set it in its own place:
phrases.notes: Here the details come from the testimony oath itself, not from the deposit oath.

phrases.english: Just as one who is made to swear by others,

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית דִּין אִין, שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין לָא;
phrases.english: in court, yes, he is liable; not in court, no.
so too one who swears on his own,

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית דִּין אִין, שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין לָא.
phrases.english: in court, yes; not in court, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side, in contrast to רבי מאיר's view in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, a witness who swears on his own is liable only if he swore in בית דין, just like one who is made to swear by others.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute in the משנה comes down to whether the details come from the source (פקדון) or from the topic's own rules (עדות).
